findings.source_quote: εἰ κατὰ τὴν κραυγὴν αὐτῶν τὴν ἐρχομένην πρὸς μὲ συντελοῦνται
findings.english_quote: whether they are carrying matters through in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me
findings.issue: The draft adopts an action-oriented middle interpretation of συντελοῦνται without discussing its materially different passive interpretation. The supplied form can also express being completed or brought to an end. The main rendering is defensible, but its interpretation and the alternative are not disclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Add a source-quoted note explaining that the main text understands συντελοῦνται as carrying matters through to completion, contextually referring to conduct corresponding to the outcry. Preserve the passive alternative, approximately “whether they are being brought to an end in accordance with their outcry that is coming to me.” Explain that “matters” is an English clarification, not an expressed Greek object. The resulting revision requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: Εἰ μηδὲν ἀγαπᾷ ὁ κακὸς καὶ πάνυ μοχθηρὸς ἐφ’ οἷς ἁμαρτάνει ἑαυτὸν ἐλέγχειν, ἀπόκριναί μοι.
findings.english_quote: If an evil and utterly wicked person does not at all wish to expose himself regarding the things in which he sins, answer me.
findings.issue: The English presents a conditional instruction but does not clearly ask the question Simon subsequently answers. In context, εἰ introduces the proposition Peter asks Simon to confirm or deny; Οὐκ ἀγαπᾷ supplies that answer. The draft obscures this interrogative function and the exchange’s argumentative structure.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed replacement: “Tell me whether an evil and utterly wicked person has no desire at all to expose himself regarding the things in which he sins.” This preserves the negative proposition while making it the object of Peter’s request for an answer. The replacement requires fresh review.
